stem: Which component of a map explains what each symbol and colour stands for?

options.rationale: Correct: the key (legend) explains every symbol, colour and line style used on the map.
The scale relates map distance to ground distance; it does not explain symbols.
The frame is the border that encloses the map.
The title says what the map shows and where, not what each symbol means.

explanation: The **key** (or legend) is the panel that explains the meaning of every symbol, colour and line used on the map.

stem: On most topographical maps, what is shown in **brown**?

options.rationale: Correct: brown is the conventional colour for relief, so contours are printed in brown.
Water features are conventionally blue.
Vegetation is conventionally green.
Most buildings and railways are printed in black.

explanation: By convention **blue** = water, **brown** = relief (contours), **green** = vegetation and **black** = most human features. Always confirm with the key.

stem: Which map would show a **small area in the greatest detail**?

options.rationale: Correct: 1:25 000 is the largest scale here, so it covers the smallest area in the most detail.
1:50 000 is a smaller scale than 1:25 000, so it shows less detail.
1:250 000 is a small scale that covers a much larger area in less detail.
1:1 000 000 is an atlas (small) scale: a very large area with little detail.

explanation: The smaller the number after 1:, the **larger** the scale and the more detail shown. 1 cm on a 1:25 000 map is 250 m on the ground; on a 1:1 000 000 map it is 10 km.

stem: A road is shown on a topographical map by a line. What kind of map symbol is this?

options.rationale: Point symbols mark features at one spot, such as a school or a borehole.
Area symbols are shading or patterns that cover ground, such as forest or a built-up area.
Correct: features that run across the map, such as roads, rivers and power lines, are line symbols.
A spot height is a point symbol giving the height of the land at one place.

explanation: Symbols are **point** (one place), **line** (features with length) or **area** (features covering ground). A road is a line symbol.

stem: Which type of map would best show the boundaries of the provinces of Zimbabwe and their capitals?

options.rationale: A relief (physical) map shows the height of the land, not administrative boundaries.
Correct: political maps show countries, provinces, boundaries and administrative centres.
A topographical sheet covers a small area in detail; it is not used to show a whole country's provinces.
A climate map shows temperature, rainfall or climate zones.

explanation: **Political maps** show human-made divisions: international and provincial boundaries and capitals.

stem: A pupil's sketch map of the route from home to school has a title, a key and a frame. Which addition would let a stranger **turn the map to match the ground**?

options.rationale: These tell the reader who drew the map and when, not which way it faces.
Grid lines help to give references, but without a north point the map still cannot be oriented.
Correct: a north point shows direction, so the map can be oriented to match the land.
A title describes the map's content; it does not give direction.

explanation: Orienting a map means turning it so that north on the map faces north on the ground; that requires a **north point**.

stem: Why is it important for a map to give its **source and date**?

options.content: So the reader can measure distances between places on it
options.rationale: Distances are measured with the scale, not the date.

options.content: So the reader can find north on it
options.rationale: Direction comes from the north point.

options.content: So the reader can work out the heights of hills on it
options.rationale: Heights come from contours and spot heights.

options.content: So the reader can judge how current it is
options.rationale: Correct: features such as roads and settlements change, so the date shows whether the map is current.

explanation: A map is a record at one time. A map surveyed long ago may not show a new road or a growing settlement, so the **source and date** help the reader judge its reliability.

stem:
**Map extract A** (fictional area), scale 1:50 000, grid squares 1 km, contour interval 20 m.

| N \ E | 61 | 62 | 63 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 45 | Green tree symbols across the square; brown contour lines 1 420 m and 1 440 m | Black square marked Sch at 624 457; black square marked Cl at 627 452 | Blue line with arrow flowing south-east; small blue circle marked BH at 638 456 |
| 44 | Red line running W-E (main road); black cross symbol marked Ch at 616 443 | Small black squares clustered along the red road | Blue area marked Dam at 634 446; dashed black line (footpath) to the dam |

Which feature is located at grid reference **627 452**?

options.rationale: The school (Sch) is at 624 457, in the same square but further north-west.
Correct: square 6245 contains a black square marked Cl at 627 452, a clinic.
The church (Ch) is at 616 443, in square 6144.
The borehole (BH) is at 638 456, in square 6345.

explanation: 627 452 is 7 tenths east of easting 62 and 2 tenths north of northing 45, in square 6245. The symbol there is marked **Cl**, the usual abbreviation for a clinic.
hints: Find easting 62 and northing 45: the square to the right of line 62 and above line 45.
Read the abbreviations in that square: Sch and Cl.

stem:
**Map extract A** (fictional area), scale 1:50 000, grid squares 1 km, contour interval 20 m.

| N \ E | 61 | 62 | 63 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 45 | Green tree symbols across the square; brown contour lines 1 420 m and 1 440 m | Black square marked Sch at 624 457; black square marked Cl at 627 452 | Blue line with arrow flowing south-east; small blue circle marked BH at 638 456 |
| 44 | Red line running W-E (main road); black cross symbol marked Ch at 616 443 | Small black squares clustered along the red road | Blue area marked Dam at 634 446; dashed black line (footpath) to the dam |

Which statement is best supported by the evidence in the extract?

options.content: The settlement in square 6244 is mainly a mining town.
options.rationale: No mine, dump or shaft symbol appears in the extract.

options.content: The area around the dam is used for a large forest plantation.
options.rationale: The forest symbols are in square 6145, not around the dam in 6344.

options.content: The settlement in square 6244 provides some services to the surrounding area.
options.rationale: Correct: a school, a clinic and a church are close to the settlement, which is evidence of a service function.

options.content: The river in square 6345 flows towards the north-west.
options.rationale: The arrow on the river shows it flows towards the south-east.

explanation: Evidence of function must come from symbols on the map. A **school, a clinic and a church** near the clustered houses show that the settlement provides education, health and religious services.
hints: Look for symbols of buildings that serve people: schools, clinics, churches.
Check each option against the squares named in it.

stem: A sketch map must be drawn exactly to scale.
explanation: False. A sketch map is drawn freehand and only approximately to scale. It still needs a title, key and north arrow, and often an approximate scale such as *about 1 cm to 200 m*.

stem: Match each map component with its purpose.

right.content: Allow the position of features to be given by references
States what the map shows and where
Relates distances on the map to distances on the ground
Shows direction so the map can be oriented

explanation: Each component has a job: **scale** for distance, **north point** for direction, **grid lines** for location and **title** for subject and place.

stem: Complete the sentence about map colours.

payload.template: On most topographical maps, rivers and dams are shown in {{blank:a}} and forests in {{blank:b}}.

explanation: Water features are **blue** and vegetation is **green**; brown is used for relief and black for most human features.

stem: Give the other name for the **key** of a map (one word).
explanation: The key is also called the **legend**.

stem: Describe **three** differences between a topographical map and a sketch map.

points.description: States that a topographical map is drawn accurately to a stated scale while a sketch map is only roughly to scale.
States that a topographical map shows many features (relief, drainage, vegetation, human features) while a sketch map shows only the features needed for its purpose.
States that a topographical map is surveyed/printed with conventional symbols and grid lines while a sketch map is drawn freehand with simple symbols (often without a grid).

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A topographical map is drawn accurately to scale, but a sketch map is only roughly to scale. A topographical map shows many kinds of feature, while a sketch map shows only those needed for one purpose. A topographical map is surveyed and printed with standard symbols and a grid; a sketch map is drawn freehand.

explanation: Topographical maps are accurate, detailed, surveyed and gridded; sketch maps are freehand, simplified and drawn for one purpose.

stem: A Form 2 group must draw a sketch map to guide visitors from the bus stop to their school. Describe **four** things they should do so that the map is useful.

points.description: Gives the map a title stating its purpose, e.g. *Route from the bus stop to the school*.
Adds a north arrow (and a frame).
Draws the route clearly and shows only useful landmarks, e.g. junctions, a bridge, a shop, a church.
Uses simple symbols explained in a key (and an approximate scale).

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Give it a clear title. Add a north arrow and a frame. Draw the route from the bus stop first and add only landmarks a stranger would notice, such as the bridge, the shop and the road junction. Use simple symbols, explain them in a key and add an approximate scale.

explanation: A sketch map is useful when it is clear, oriented, focused on its purpose and explained by a key.
hints: Think of the components of a good map.
Think about which features to leave out.

stem: A district council wants a map to plan where to drill new boreholes in its rural wards. Discuss whether a **topographical map** at 1:50 000 is more useful for this task than a **small-scale political map** of Zimbabwe.

points.description: Explains that the 1:50 000 map shows rivers, dams, existing boreholes and wells, so gaps in water supply can be identified.
Explains that it shows settlements, schools and clinics, so boreholes can be placed near the people who need them.
Explains that contours/relief help to judge access for drilling rigs and the likely flow of groundwater towards valleys.
Explains that a political map is small scale and shows only boundaries and main centres, so it cannot show individual villages or water points.
Reaches a judgement (e.g. the topographical map is far more useful, though the political map helps to see ward and district boundaries; the topographical map may be out of date).

levels.descriptor: Developed, accurate explanation of several relevant points, supported by a located example or the resource, with a clear judgement or conclusion where the question asks for one.
Some explanation of relevant points, partly developed; an example or resource evidence is used in general terms; any judgement is simple or one-sided.
Simple statements or a list of points with little explanation; no example or only a name.

answerSpec.modelAnswer: The 1:50 000 topographical map is far more useful. It is large scale, so it shows rivers, dams and existing boreholes, letting planners see which villages are far from water. It also shows the settlements, schools and clinics that need water, and its contours show valleys where groundwater may collect and slopes that rigs must climb. A small-scale political map shows only provincial and district boundaries and main towns, so individual wards and water points do not appear. It might help to confirm which ward is the council's responsibility, but it cannot be used to choose sites. The planners should, however, check the date of the topographical map, because new settlements and boreholes may have appeared since it was surveyed.

explanation: A large-scale map shows the detail needed for local planning; small-scale maps give the regional picture only.
hints: What detail does each map show?
Which features matter for siting boreholes: rivers, settlements, relief?

stem:
**Map extract A** (fictional area), scale 1:50 000, grid squares 1 km, contour interval 20 m.

| N \ E | 61 | 62 | 63 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 45 | Green tree symbols across the square; brown contour lines 1 420 m and 1 440 m | Black square marked Sch at 624 457; black square marked Cl at 627 452 | Blue line with arrow flowing south-east; small blue circle marked BH at 638 456 |
| 44 | Red line running W-E (main road); black cross symbol marked Ch at 616 443 | Small black squares clustered along the red road | Blue area marked Dam at 634 446; dashed black line (footpath) to the dam |

Answer the questions about the extract.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: What is shown by the brown lines in square 6145?

options.rationale: The footpath is a dashed black line in square 6344.
Rivers are blue lines.
Boundaries are normally black broken lines and have no heights.
Correct: brown lines with heights (1 420 m, 1 440 m) are contours.

parts.explanation: Brown lines labelled with heights are contours, joining places of equal height.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Name the natural vegetation shown in square 6145.
parts.explanation: Green tree symbols show forest or woodland.

parts.label: (c)
parts.explanation: The blue area marked Dam at 634 446 is a dam (reservoir).

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Using evidence from the extract only, describe how the people living in square 6244 obtain water, education and health care.

points.description: Water: from the dam at 634 446 (reached by the footpath) and/or the borehole at 638 456.

parts.explanation: Each service must be linked to a symbol on the map and, ideally, its grid reference.

explanation: Map reading starts with the key: colours and abbreviations identify features, and evidence for an answer must be quoted from the extract.
hints: Each square is named by the easting to its left and the northing below it.
Use the colours: blue water, green vegetation, brown relief.

stem: A Form 1 learner, Chipo, has drawn a map of her village. It has a frame, a key and a title, *My village*. It shows huts, a borehole, a store and a river. It has no north arrow and no scale.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: What kind of map has Chipo drawn?

options.rationale: Topographical maps are surveyed and printed accurately to scale.
Correct: a freehand map of a local area drawn for a purpose is a sketch map.
A choropleth map shades areas according to a statistic.
A political map shows boundaries and capitals.

parts.explanation: A freehand map of the local area drawn without accurate measurement is a sketch map.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Name **two** components of a good map that are missing from Chipo's map.

points.description: Scale (an approximate scale such as 1 cm to 100 m).

parts.explanation: Her map has a title, frame and key but no north point or scale.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain why each of the missing components matters to someone using the map.

points.description: Without a north arrow the user cannot orient the map or give directions from it.
Without a scale the user cannot estimate how far apart features are or how long a walk will take.

parts.explanation: Direction and distance are two of the main things a reader takes from a map.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: True or false: the borehole on Chipo's map is a point symbol.
parts.explanation: True. A borehole is at one place, so it is shown by a point symbol.

explanation: Sketch maps still need the basic components of a good map: title, frame, key, north point and approximate scale.
hints: Which components of a good map are missing?
How would a stranger know which way to hold it?

stem: Which feature would most likely be shown on a topographical map by an **area symbol**?

options.rationale: A railway has length but little width on the map: a line symbol.
A borehole is at one spot: a point symbol.
A trig station is a single surveyed point: a point symbol.
Correct: a plantation covers ground, so it is shown by area shading or a pattern.

explanation: Area symbols (shading, tints or repeated patterns) cover features with extent, such as forests, cultivation, swamps and built-up areas.
